A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same column-normalized guidance method and low-dimensional analysis. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, guidance-schedule evaluations, and conditional molecular-generation results on QM9.

after.justification: V2 retains original ImageNet and QM9 results and adds GenEval, MATH-500, and precision–recall evaluations.

M1.justification: The central masked-diffusion softmax rule and Listings 1–2 remain unchanged. However, the general-case pseudocode changes from geometrically combining scores in v1 Listing 3 to applying softmax to jump probabilities and exponentiating combined rates in v2 Listing 4. These operations are not equivalent as written and conflict with the stated formulation, leaving an intended method revision versus erroneous pseudocode unresolved.

E1.justification: V2 adds text-conditioned image generation on GenEval using Meissonic and Show-o, and mathematical text generation on MATH-500 using LLaDA-8B-Instruct. ImageNet, QM9, and the synthetic example remain; uniform-QM9 evaluation moves to Appendix E rather than being removed.

E2.justification: The shared ImageNet and uniform-QM9 experiments retain Unlocking and Simple Guidance. V2 adds a separately reported masked-QM9 comparison containing Simple Guidance alone, while its GenEval tables compare against Unlocking alone. These introduce limited changes in comparator participation without introducing a new guidance baseline family.

E3.justification: V2 introduces GenEval evaluation, precision–recall measurement, and a MATH-500 protocol using up to 256 generated tokens, 32-token blocks, and 32 Euler steps per block without remasking. Table 2 also reverses the reported Ramp-Up and Ramp-Down formulas relative to v1. The retained ImageNet sample counts, samplers, and Figure 6 values do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a dedicated fidelity–diversity analysis through precision–recall curves and expands qualitative guidance-strength comparisons to text-to-image generation. Appendix F also reports an additional masked-QM9 analysis, although its contradictory uniform-diffusion description and reused curves limit interpretation. The original schedule analysis remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports numerical repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Generic references to samples across seeds or configurations do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds GenEval scores, MATH-500 outcomes, and precision–recall results while retaining ImageNet Figure 6 values. Meissonic scores 45.9 versus Unlocking's 28.5 at guidance 6, but 40.8 versus 43.1 at guidance 3. Uniform-QM9 Figure 11 omits intermediate points from v1 Figure 7. The additional Figure 12 reproduces Simple/Unlocking curves from Figure 11 while relabeling the latter as Ours, making that result attribution uncertain.

T1.justification: Most theory survives relocation: v1 Theorem 3.2 becomes v2 Theorem B.2, Lemma 2.1 becomes Lemma A.1, and the two-dimensional corollary and proofs remain. V2 introduces an explicit jump-rate/jump-distribution decomposition but drops v1 Theorem 3.3's standalone normalized piecewise-guidance statement. This is a limited revision rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: V2 refocuses the title and abstract on low-dimensional masked-diffusion insights with image and text applications, replacing v1's prominent claim of empirical applicability to any discrete diffusion. It also explicitly claims the first theoretical characterization of guidance schedules. The central normalization contribution and preference for stronger later guidance remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretation of the fidelity–diversity tradeoff and explains normalization through separating jump frequency from jump destination. It explicitly qualifies the comparability of its LLaDA results because of the controlled sampler without remasking. The low-dimensional theoretical limitations and weaker uniform-QM9 conclusions are retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies implementation settings for the new LLaDA evaluation and substantially rewrites the general-case pseudocode when moving it from Appendix A to Appendix E. The rewrite introduces inconsistencies with the mathematical formulation. Existing toy-data construction and the eight-A100 hardware disclosure remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting GenEval, Meissonic, LLaDA, Show-o, and newer diffusion-language applications. It removes the Halton-sampler discussion and its Besnier and MaskGIT citations, including v1's acknowledgment that earlier logit interpolation closely resembles the proposed method. The principal guidance references remain.

P1.justification: The preliminaries and normalization explanation are extensively rewritten, including an expanded CFG introduction and a simpler main-text theoretical presentation. Experiments are reorganized around normalization and schedules, QM9 moves to the appendices, and new appendix sections separate general diffusion, molecular experiments, and image galleries. These are substantial narrative changes beyond added results.

P2.justification: V2 adds precision–recall and MATH-500 plots, GenEval heatmaps, two detailed score tables, and extensive text-to-image comparison grids. Existing figures are relocated or redrawn, and Figure 6's interval legends are corrected. The original ImageNet sample grids are retained in Appendix H.

improvement.justification: The new GenEval and MATH-500 evaluations, fidelity–diversity analysis, and clearer organization strengthen the paper's empirical scope and accessibility. However, v2 introduces unresolved implementation and reporting problems: Listing 4 conflicts with the stated normalization rule, Figure 9's category labels disagree with Tables 3–4, and Figure 12 reuses curves under changed method labels while its setup contradicts itself about masked versus uniform diffusion. These problems prevent a confident judgment that the expanded evidence yields a net overall quality improvement.
